sources.section: Boiling cloudy drinking water: chemical contamination and elevation limits
sources.text:
Follow local public-health advice about the water supply. Use safe bottled water if available. Water contaminated with fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactive material cannot be made safe by boiling or disinfecting it; obtain a different safe supply.

When the concern is germs and safe bottled water is unavailable, first pass cloudy water through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter, or allow it to settle and draw off the clear water. Bring the clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 6,500 feet elevation, boil for 3 minutes. Let it cool and store it in clean, sanitized containers with tight covers.

This boiling summary does not provide a bleach dose; product ingredients and concentration must be known before using a product-specific disinfection procedure.

Source: [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://www.cdc.gov/water-emergency/about/index.html) — Water with fuel or toxic chemicals in it; Steps for boiling water; companion one-page fact sheet. Edition: Supporting page September 19, 2024; fact-sheet listing August 28, 2024. Scope: General public. Region: United States source; follow local public-health advice.

sources.original_text: If water may contain fuel or toxic chemicals, do not drink it. Boiling or adding disinfectant cannot make water containing fuel or toxic chemicals safe. Obtain bottled water or another safe supply and contact local health authorities for advice.

sources.doc_title: Water: finding, purifying and storing it
sources.text:
- Food-grade containers, clean and with lids; never reuse chemical containers.
- Store in a dark, cool place. Replace stored water every 6 months or treat it again.
- For every 1,000 liters of cistern water, the common maintenance dose is about 100 mL of 2.5% bleach, waiting 30 minutes (follow local health authority guidance).
- Draw water with a ladle or tap, without dipping hands or mugs in.
